hints.title: Subarray Window Constraint
hints.text: Every subarray of length 3 must have at least one element >= k, meaning among any 3 consecutive indices i, i+1, i+2, at least one must be incremented to >= k.

hints.title: Dynamic Programming State
hints.text: Let dp[i] be the minimum increment cost such that nums[i] is raised to at least k and all triplets up to i are satisfied.

hints.title: Transition from Recent Pivot
hints.text: To satisfy triplet constraints, the previous chosen pivot must be at index i - 1, i - 2, or i - 3. Hence dp[i] = max(0, k - nums[i]) + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2], dp[i-3]).

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy choice without looking 3 steps ahead can overpay for future triplets.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) extra space with rolling variables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulate DP using previous 3 indices as legal antecedents.
